title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery

data.title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery
data.research_question: Does a simple attribution-patching-based method outperform existing automated circuit discovery methods, and what are its limitations?

models_and_data.item: Indirect Object Identification (IOI), Docstring, and Greater-Than tasks
models_and_data.quote: We compare Edge Attribution Patching (EAP) and ACDC on the Indirect Object Identification (IOI), Docstring, and Greater-Than tasks.

models_and_data.item: GPT-2 small models used for IOI and Greater-Than
models_and_data.quote: Activation patching was not included in the other tasks as it was too computationally expensive to run on the GPT-2 small models used by IOI and Greater-Than.
For each of these tasks, previous studies identified a subgraph (circuit) relevant for solving the task.
We use the docstring task as a case study due to the small model size used.

protocol.step: Define activation patching as replacing activations from one forward pass with activations from a different forward pass.
protocol.quote: Activation patching refers to replacing the activations from one model forward pass with the activations from a different forward pass.

protocol.step: Use attribution patching to estimate activation patching effects for many edges with two forward passes and one backward pass.
protocol.quote: Attribution patching [20] is a technique for estimating Equation (1) for many different edges E using only two forward passes and one backward pass.

protocol.step: Run EAP by computing absolute attribution scores for all edges, sorting them, and keeping the top k edges.
protocol.quote: i) use Equation (2) to obtain absolute attribution scores for the importance of all edges in the computational graph and then ii) sort these scores and keep the top k edges in a circuit.

protocol.step: Compare EAP and ACDC on IOI, Docstring, and Greater-Than tasks.
protocol.quote: We compare Edge Attribution Patching (EAP) and ACDC on the Indirect Object Identification (IOI), Docstring, and Greater-Than tasks.

protocol.step: Run EAP first, then ACDC on the pruned subgraph for the Docstring task.
protocol.quote: We ran EAP first, then ACDC on the resulting subgraph for the Docstring task, varying pruning thresholds for EAP and ACDC independently.

protocol.step: Use task-specific metrics rather than KL divergence to avoid zero-gradient issues.
protocol.quote: In this work we use the ‘task-specific metrics’ (not KL divergence) from [10] so avoid this issue.

key_results.claim: EAP achieved AUC 0.904 on the IOI task.
EAP achieved AUC 0.896 on the Greater-Than task.
EAP achieved AUC 0.976 on the Docstring task.
ACDC with KL divergence achieved AUC 0.982 on the Docstring task, outperforming EAP there.
EAP requires just two forward passes and a backward pass.
key_results.numbers: two forward passes and a backward pass
key_results.quote: requiring just two forward passes and a backward pass.

key_results.claim: Attribution patching scores have a weak correlation with activation patching scores, R2 = 0.27.
key_results.quote: we find a fairly weak correlation between activation and attribution patching scores (R2 = 0.27).

key_results.claim: Combining EAP then ACDC increased performance compared to EAP only.
key_results.quote: The combined methods show increased performance compared to EAP only.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Attribution patching fails when the metric gradient is the zero vector.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: one limitation of attribution patching is that it will not work when the gradient of the metric is the zero vector.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Attribution patching approximations correlate only weakly with activation patching scores.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: we find a fairly weak correlation between activation and attribution patching scores (R2 = 0.27).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Attribution patching can overestimate the effect of activation patching.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: suggesting that attribution patching estimates the effect of activation patching as twice as important as it really is.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The linear approximation is inaccurate for some docstring circuit edges.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Figure 4b shows the result for one edge in the docstring circuit where the linear approximation to activation patching is not accurate.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Interpretability metrics do not precisely capture meaningful human understanding.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: the metrics used for interpretability do not precisely capture meaningful human understanding.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Human-found circuits are imperfect and add noise to evaluation.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: human-found circuits are imperfect, increasing the noise in this measurement.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: EAP is evaluated on GPT-2 small and a small docstring model, not on Gemma 4 E2B; transfer to KV-shared layers 15-34 and per-layer embeddings is untested.
The edge-level computational graph may not directly represent KV-sharing or per-layer embedding pathways, so attribution scores could miss or misattribute importance in those components.
AUC against prior human circuits is a proxy; it does not establish causal faithfulness for induction-head or factual-recall tracing.
The linear approximation can fail for nonlinear or concave effects, especially embedding edges, which may misrank edges in factual-recall tasks.
The paper does not test CPU-only feasibility or memory/runtime for large models; backward passes on Gemma 4 E2B may be costly.
Top-k and threshold selection are only lightly explored, and the EAP+ACDC combination is tested only on the Docstring task.
data.relevance_to_lab: EAP is directly relevant as a cheap edge-attribution and circuit-discovery baseline for Gemma 4 E2B activation patching, logit lens, induction-head, and factual-recall tracing; however, the paper does not address KV-shared layers, per-layer embeddings, or CPU constraints.

data.title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery
data.research_question: Does Edge Attribution Patching recover task-relevant model circuits more accurately and efficiently than activation-patching-based ACDC and other automated circuit-discovery methods, and how faithful are its edge-level attribution scores to activation patching?

models_and_data.quote: For each of these tasks, previous studies identified a subgraph (circuit) relevant for solving the task. We use their results as a ground truth for benchmarking both methods.
In this work we always compute this score across a set of (xclean , xcorr ) pairs and take the mean.

protocol.step: Represent each language model as a directed acyclic computational graph.
protocol.quote: We view language models as directed, acyclic graphs.

protocol.step: Compute attribution information for many candidate edges using two forward passes and one backward pass.
protocol.quote: Attribution patching [20] is a technique for estimating Equation (1) for many different edges E using only two forward passes and one backward pass.

protocol.step: Linearly approximate activation-patching effects with a first-order Taylor expansion of the task metric.
protocol.quote: It linearly approximates the metric difference after corrupting a single edge in the computational graph (Figure 1) by expanding L as a function of the edge activation as a Taylor series with terms up to the first order:

protocol.step: Score all graph edges, sort the scores, and retain the top-k edges as the discovered circuit.
protocol.quote: This takes two steps: i) use Equation (2) to obtain absolute attribution scores for the importance of all edges in the computational graph and then ii) sort these scores and keep the top k edges in a circuit.

protocol.step: Use task-specific metrics rather than KL divergence for the main EAP method.
protocol.quote: In this work we use the ‘task-specific metrics’ (not KL divergence) from [10] so avoid this issue.

protocol.step: Benchmark EAP and ACDC against previous circuits on IOI, Greater-Than, and Docstring, with activation patching additionally evaluated on Docstring.
protocol.quote: We compare Edge Attribution Patching (EAP) and ACDC on the Indirect Object Identification (IOI), Docstring, and Greater-Than tasks.

protocol.step: For Docstring, run EAP first and then apply ACDC to the pruned subgraph using independently varied pruning thresholds.
protocol.quote: We ran EAP first, then ACDC on the resulting subgraph for the Docstring task, varying pruning thresholds for EAP and ACDC independently.

metrics.name: Task statistic L
metrics.definition: The model statistic measured for a task, commonly loss or logit difference.
metrics.quote: For example, L often represents loss or logit difference [3].

metrics.name: Activation-patching metric change
metrics.definition: The change in the task metric produced by replacing a clean edge activation with its corrupted counterpart, as defined by Equation (1).
metrics.quote: In this work, we use the change in metric under activation patching

metrics.name: Absolute attribution score
metrics.definition: The magnitude of the first-order attribution score, used as the approximation to activation-patching impact.
metrics.quote: A simple rearrangement implies that Equation (1) is approximately equal to |∆e L| (3) which we call the absolute attribution score for the rest of this paper.

metrics.name: Mean absolute attribution score
metrics.definition: The absolute attribution score averaged over clean-corrupted prompt pairs.
metrics.quote: In this work we always compute this score across a set of (xclean , xcorr ) pairs and take the mean.

metrics.name: ROC AUC
metrics.definition: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for ranking circuit edges against the benchmark ground truth.
metrics.quote: The ROC curves in Figure 2 suggest the performance of EAP is better than ACDC overall: it has the maximal AUC in Figure 2a-2b, while ACDC used with the KL Divergence metric outperforms EAP in Figure 2c.

metrics.name: KL divergence
metrics.definition: An alternative ACDC metric that is nonnegative and equals zero at the unablated model, causing all gradients there to be zero.
metrics.quote: Conmy et al. [10] recommended the use of KL divergence as a metric, which is i) equal to 0 when we run the model without ablations and ii) a non-negative metric.

metrics.name: Youdens-J statistic
metrics.definition: The maximum true-positive rate minus false-positive rate.
metrics.quote: Youdens-J statistic (maximum TPR minus FPR value) for combining EAP and ACDC methods on the docstring task.

metrics.name: R2
metrics.definition: The goodness-of-fit measure for the relationship between activation-patching and attribution-patching scores.
metrics.quote: Surprisingly, we find a fairly weak correlation between activation and attribution patching scores (R2 = 0.27).

key_results.claim: EAP had the highest reported circuit-recovery AUC on IOI.
key_results.numbers: EAP Only AUC = 0.904; ACDC w/ IOI Metric AUC = 0.588; ACDC w/ KL Divergence Metric AUC = 0.868

key_results.claim: EAP had the highest reported circuit-recovery AUC on Greater-Than.
key_results.numbers: EAP Only AUC = 0.896; ACDC w/ GreaterThan Metric AUC = 0.458; ACDC w/ KL Divergence Metric AUC = 0.849

key_results.claim: On Docstring, EAP slightly trailed Activation Patching and ACDC with KL divergence while nearly matching ACDC with the task metric.
key_results.numbers: EAP Only AUC = 0.976; Activation Patching AUC = 0.978; ACDC w/ Docstring Metric AUC = 0.972; ACDC w/ KL Divergence metric AUC = 0.982
key_results.quote: The ROC curves in Figure 2 suggest the performance of EAP is better than ACDC overall: it has the maximal AUC in Figure 2a-2b, while ACDC used with the KL Divergence metric outperforms EAP in Figure 2c.

key_results.claim: EAP estimated effects for many edges using two forward passes and one backward pass, while ACDC's required forward-pass count scaled exponentially with graph size.
key_results.numbers: two forward passes and one backward pass
key_results.quote: Attribution patching [20] is a technique for estimating Equation (1) for many different edges E using only two forward passes and one backward pass.

key_results.claim: Applying ACDC after EAP pruning improved circuit recovery over EAP alone on Docstring.
key_results.quote: The combined methods show increased performance compared to EAP only.

key_results.claim: Attribution-patching and activation-patching scores had a weak correspondence.
key_results.quote: Surprisingly, we find a fairly weak correlation between activation and attribution patching scores (R2 = 0.27).

key_results.claim: The best-fit slope indicated that EAP estimated activation-patching effects as twice as large.
key_results.quote: Moreover, the line of best fit has gradient 0.531, suggesting that attribution patching estimates the effect of activation patching as twice as important as it really is.

key_results.claim: Only six edges outside the IOI circuit had attribution scores outside the reported central interval.
key_results.quote: Furthermore, there are only 6 edges outside of the interval [−0.25, 0.25] that aren’t part of the IOI circuit.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Attribution patching cannot work when the metric gradient is the zero vector.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Note that one limitation of attribution patching is that it will not work when the gradient of the metric is the zero vector.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The first-order attribution scores are only weakly correlated with activation-patching scores.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Surprisingly, we find a fairly weak correlation between activation and attribution patching scores (R2 = 0.27).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: For nonlinear, concave corruption paths, the linear approximation can substantially overestimate the actual effect.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We find that interpolating towards the corrupted input creates a concave curve (Figure 4b) such that the linear approximation at λ = 0 overestimates the effect of activation patching this edge.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The documented additional approximation failures involve edges originating from positional or token embeddings.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: These cases all involve an edge that comes from the model’s embeddings (positional and tokens).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The interpretability metrics do not precisely capture meaningful human understanding.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Finally, one further limitation of this research is that the metrics used for interpretability do not precisely capture meaningful human understanding.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Ground-truth recovery is difficult for not-yet-understood tasks, and previously found human circuits introduce measurement noise.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Recovering a subgraph that humans previously recovered is limited because i) we can’t evaluate this metric for interpretability tasks that we don’t yet understand and ii) human-found circuits are imperfect, increasing the noise in this measurement.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: A direct activation-patching comparison was omitted for IOI and Greater-Than because it was too computationally expensive.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Activation patching was not included in the other tasks as it was too computationally expensive to run on the GPT-2 small models used by IOI and Greater-Than.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The detailed approximation case study used the small-model Docstring task.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We use the docstring task as a case study due to the small model size used.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The evaluation does not include Gemma 4 E2B, shared-KV architectures, or models of comparable scale, so EAP ranking quality in the lab setting is unverified.
No CPU-specific runtime, peak-memory, or backward-pass resource measurements are reported; counting forward and backward passes alone may hide substantial memory and kernel costs.
Only three narrow benchmarks and small models are studied, leaving task- and scale-generalization unestablished.
No repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported for the AUC differences.
Ground-truth circuit overlap is the primary endpoint; the paper does not independently establish that recovered subgraphs are causally sufficient for behavior on held-out inputs.
Shared-KV query, key, and value pathways are not treated explicitly, so attribution can be ambiguous when several components interact through shared paths.
The study does not validate per-layer embeddings as an interpretability object or reproduce factual-recall and induction-head tracing protocols.
Threshold selection and known-circuit benchmarking may favor methods tuned to the evaluation topology; no held-out circuit or newly discovered circuit is used as an end-to-end benchmark.
data.relevance_to_lab: The paper provides a directly relevant cheap-first-pass method: EAP estimates graph-edge importance with two forward passes and one backward pass, and the authors recommend running EAP before ACDC. For Gemma 4 E2B, instantiate a computational graph for the KV-shared paths in layers 15-34 and per-layer embedding activations, then use task-specific metrics such as logit difference to avoid the zero-gradient problem identified with KL divergence at the clean baseline. Use EAP rankings to pre-prune candidate edges, then confirm high-scoring edges with activation patching, logit lens, induction-head tracing, and factual-recall tracing rather than treating the ranking as causal proof. The paper reports neither CPU resource measurements nor shared-KV or per-layer-embedding validation, so those remain lab-specific work.
